items.question: Is 'kr >= 30' THEIR kernel converging to Mie, or a bound on ours?
items.verdict: VERIFIED - and it is THEIRS, describing THEIR PEC-sphere validation. It is NOT a bound on our kernel.

evidence.quote: Figure 4: Frequency scan of monostatic RCS for a triangulated PEC sphere, averaged across incident directions. The results highlight the Mie resonance region where ray tracing is inapplicable, followed by the optical region where the method accurately approximates scattering with a standard deviation of ∼2.5%. At higher frequencies, a low ray density region fails to resolve the wavelength, leading to an aliasing instability. The labels kr = 30 and kr = 8000 denote the boundary of the optical region and the onset of the aliasing instability, respectively.

Electrical size is here defined as kr = 2πr/λ, where r is the sphere radius. At kr = 1, Mie resonances dominate and ray tracing methods fail, as wave effects cannot be neglected in this regime. Ray-based approximations become valid as frequency increases, with good agreement typically expected for kr ≳ 30.

Our simulation results (Fig. 4) demonstrate excellent agreement with Mie theory beginning at an electrical size around kr ≈ 30. This transition marks the boundary between the Mie resonance region, where wave phenomena dominate, and the optical region, where the ray approximation can accurately capture the scattering physics of the triangulated PEC sphere.

In our simulations, this phenomenon occurs at electrical sizes around kr ≈ 8 × 10³. To explicitly demonstrate the onset of aliasing, the ray grid density was held strictly constant throughout this specific frequency sweep experiment. As the wavelength decreased at higher frequencies, the static Δs eventually violated the λ/5 criterion.

items.what_the_paper_says: kr >= 30 is (a) a GENERAL property of ray-based asymptotics that Sagitta restates ('typically expected'), and (b) the point where THEIR SBR curve starts matching Mie for a PEC SPHERE, monostatic, averaged over incident directions. kr = 8000 is not a physics limit at all: it is where THEIR sweep, with ray density deliberately held constant, broke their own lambda/5 rule. The 2.5% is a standard deviation of the already direction-averaged curve in the optical region (F5's self-correction is confirmed).
items.consequence: Two things follow for us. (1) kr >= 30 must never be printed as 'Sagitta says our kernel is invalid below kr=30' - it is their sphere-validation boundary, and the underlying claim is the standard Mie-to-optical transition that applies to ANY ray+PO method including ours. (2) kr = 8000 is an artefact of a fixed-grid experiment and carries no authority over our fixed-lambda-fraction grids.
items.action: Rewrite PRIOR_WORK_COMPARISON L410/L415-418/L965 to attribute the window to Sagitta's own PEC-sphere sweep, with the fixed-grid caveat for kr=8000. If we state where OUR kernel is valid, it must be our own convergence study, not a borrowed number.

evidence.quote: LAMBDA is generated on a digital-twin platform that integrates Unreal Engine 5 (UE5) [23] for high-fidelity scene construction; Cosys-AirSim [24,25] for UAV motion control and synchronized sensor support for RGB, depth, LiDAR, pose, and IMU streams; Blender [26] for scene-mesh conversion; Sionna RT [27] for material-aware ray tracing; and CADFEKO [28] for UAV radar cross-section (RCS) modeling.

The complex-valued CSI coefficient captures the propagation effects computed by the ray-tracing channel generator, whereas the RCS term is obtained from CADFEKO simulations of the AirSim UAV model and queried according to the UAV attitude.
The radar synthesis module further combines the Sionna RT multipath geometry with CADFEKO-derived UAV RCS information to generate radar data.
Altair Feko: High-frequency electromagnetic simulation software. https://altair.com/feko.

items.what_the_paper_says: LAMBDA is a textbook instance of the Q2 catalogue's 'RCS injected from an external EM solver' pattern: the mesh goes to Sionna RT for PROPAGATION only, and the target signature is computed in CADFEKO outside the ray engine and looked up by UAV attitude. This is the cleanest published statement of the split we are trying to close.

evidence.quote: The prototype uses two hardware nodes, as shown in Fig. 9. The BS employs a Luowave USRP-LW X310 connected to an Intel Core i7-10700 host over 10GbE, together with separate horn antennas for transmission and monostatic sensing reception, and an external OCXO (DAPU O23B-HCDD) as the reference clock. The UE uses a TQTT Tiny B210 connected to an Intel Core Ultra5 225H host over USB 3.0, a single omnidirectional receive antenna, and a Morion MV197 OCXO disciplined by a USB DAC.
It supports a wide range of software-defined radios, from the cost-effective USRP B200 series to the high-performance X400 series.

reasons: The 'drones, humans, and micro-Doppler as future work' sentence is in the PUBLISHED EuCAP 2025 paper (IEEE Xplore, DOI 10.23919/EuCAP63536.2025.10999367), not in a preprint. Our positioning stands behind a peer-reviewed sentence.
The one dBsm RCS from a Sionna-class engine (ZIG-CONF Fig.6) is likewise in the published version, and its target is a CAR - no drone.

The journal version, which is the only Ziganshin document that is a preprint, does NOT list drones as future work at all; its item 4 says 'time-varying substructures (micro-Doppler)' and points at Costa's drone paper. So the drone gap is not merely unclaimed, it is unclaimed in both versions.
LAMBDA now stands verified as an explicit 'RCS from CADFEKO, propagation from Sionna RT' split, which is affirmative evidence for the H8 gap rather than a counterexample.
